findings.title: Write lock does not re-check cache and can clobber a good value
findings.body: GetWebAssets drops the read lock and later takes the write lock without reading entryPointAssetsCache again. Every caller that observed a nil cache (or is running in Dev) therefore reloads the manifest while holding the global mutex, then unconditionally assigns entryPointAssetsCache = result. On a cold start, N concurrent calls all pass the nil check, queue on the write lock, and each performs a full file read; a later caller whose read fails stores nil and wipes the successful cache published by an earlier caller, so subsequent non-Dev requests miss and can return an error even though a valid asset set was already loaded. Re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock (and do not overwrite a non-nil cache with a failed load). The exclusive lock is also held across the manifest read, so those redundant loads are fully serialized.
